body_markdown:
**Store furniture during water damage repairs by moving clean, fully dry items out of affected rooms and into a temporary self-storage unit until work is completed.** A month-to-month rental from Public Storage gives you space for furniture, boxes, and household items without a long-term rental commitment.


With regular flooding in cities like Miami, Houston, New York City, Tampa, and West Palm Beach, it’s important to know how to store furniture if your home or office is affected by flooding or water damage.


Water damage repairs often disrupt more than one room, and project timelines often shift as crews inspect, dry, repair, and rebuild the space. Moving furniture out of the work area helps restoration teams access floors, walls, cabinets, and other surfaces with ease to finish the job more efficiently.


## **The Basics**


After flood or water damage in your home …


- Choose a self-storage unit that fits your current needs.


- Public Storage’s month-to-month flexibility allow your rental agreement to match the repair’s timeline and adjust to changing completion dates.


- Use Drive-Up Access for heavier furniture and easy loading.


- Review the


[Public Storage Size Guide](https://www.publicstorage.com/size-guide) to determine the storage unit size you need.


- Move


**clean, fully dry** furniture and household items into self-storage.


- Photograph and inventory furniture and clean items as recommended by a professional before they’re stored.


### **Separate Dry Items from Affected Items**


To begin restoring your space after flood or water damage, start by separating furniture and household items into clear groups—cleaning required, ready to move, or ready to move to another part of the home. Restoration professionals can help identify which items are dry and ready to pack away, which items require professional cleaning or drying, and which items you should remove from the space.


Do not place wet furniture, damp rugs, wet boxes, or other moisture-affected items into self-storage. Wet items can create odors, mold, and mildew.


**Item Condition & Next Step**


**What To Do**


Clean & Fully Dry


Pack and move into a self-storage unit


Damp or Wet


Keep out of self-storage until a restoration professional confirms the item is fully dry


Needs Cleaning or Repair


Follow guidance from your restoration or cleaning professional


No Longer Usable


Follow local disposal guidance or work with your restoration team


### **Make Room for Restoration Work**


To prepare your space for restoration work after a flood or water damage, start by clearing furniture and household items from the repair area before work begins. Focus first on pieces that limit access to floors, walls, cabinets, and built-in fixtures.


Common items to move include:


- Sofas, chairs, tables, and bookcases


- Beds, dressers, and nightstands


- Area rugs and décor


- Boxes from closets, cabinets, and storage areas


Moving these items allows restoration crews to work more efficiently and keeps your home easier to navigate during repairs. Consider utilizing a temporary self-storage unit to store these items so they’re fully out of the way of the work being done. Using a storage unit to store furniture during renovations or restorations also keeps furniture from potential damage and away from construction dust and debris.


### **Enjoy a Month-to-Month Rental Agreement**


Water damage repair timelines often change due to slow construction progress, unexpected mold discoveries, or other unforeseen factors. Drying, inspections, material availability, and follow-up work can also extend a project beyond the original estimate.


With unforeseen delays, Public Storage’s


**month-to-month rentals** allow you to


rent storage while repairs move forward and end the rental when you no longer need the space—no long term commitment required and easy extensions when you need them. Customers can also complete a storage rental online in minutes, no credit card required.


Use the


[Public Storage location finder](https://www.publicstorage.com/locations) to compare nearby facilities, unit sizes, and available features to find a unit to fit your needs and timeline.


### **Choose the Right Unit Size & Features**


The right self-storage unit for you depends on the number of rooms affected by the water damage that you’re remediating, the size of the furniture you need to relocate, and how often you expect to access the unit. Measure the larger furniture pieces and count boxes and use the


[Public Storage Size Guide](https://www.publicstorage.com/size-guide) before reserving.


**Unit Size & Storage Need**


**Typical Fit**


**5′ x 5′**


Boxes, smaller furniture, and household items from a closet or small area


**5′ x 10′**


Furniture and boxes from one room


**10′ x 10′**


Furniture and boxes from several rooms


**10′ x 15′ or Larger**


Larger furniture and household items from a multi-room repair project


For especially heavy or bulky furniture, look for


[Drive-Up Access](https://www.publicstorage.com/self-storage/drive-up-storage) which will make loading and unloading easier. Drive-Up Access lets you pull your vehicle near select ground-level units, which streamlines moving larger items. More than 45% of Public Storage properties offer Drive-Up Access.


For select household items or furniture made from wood, leather, or natural materials that require more consistent temperature or humidity levels, consider


[climate-controlled storage](https://www.publicstorage.com/climate-controlled-storage) . More than 90% of Public Storage properties offer climate-controlled units. Features, unit types, and availability vary by location.


### **Pack Furniture for Temporary Storage**


While making repairs after water or flood damage, pack your furniture and items to get them out of the way with the repair timeline in mind. You may need to retrieve items quickly when repairs finish, so label containers clearly and keep an aisle through the unit.


Follow these steps:


- Clean and dry furniture before loading it into the unit.


- Remove table legs, shelves, and other detachable pieces when practical.


- Put screws and hardware in labeled bags, then attach the bag to the matching item.


- Cover furniture with moving blankets, furniture covers, or clean sheets.


- Place heavier furniture and boxes on the floor.


- Stack lighter labeled bins on top or on shelving.


- Keep frequently needed items near the entrance.


- Leave a walkway from the door to the back of the unit.


Create a simple inventory list that notes each item, its condition, and its location in the unit. Photos also help you remember how furniture and boxes were arranged before the repairs began.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **How Do I Store My Furniture During Water Damage Repairs?**


**You should store your furniture during water damage repairs by moving clean, fully dry items out of affected rooms and into a temporary self-storage unit to keep it out of the way of construction.** Ask your restoration professional to identify furniture that needs cleaning, drying, repair, or disposal before you pack.


### **Can I Put Wet Furniture in a Self-Storage Unit?**


**You should not put wet furniture in a self-storage unit.** Dry furniture completely and follow guidance from a restoration professional before packing it away, since wet items can create odors, mold, and mildew.


### **How Long Should I Rent a Storage Unit During Repairs?**


**You should rent a storage unit during repairs for as long as the restoration work requires;** luckily


Public Storage offers month-to-month rentals, so you can keep your unit while work continues and end the rental when your home is ready.


### **What Size Storage Unit Do I Need for Furniture During Repairs?**


**You should choose a storage unit size by seeing how many rooms you need to clear, measuring your furniture, and counting boxes that need to be moved.** A 5′ x 10′ unit often fits furniture and boxes from one room, while larger projects often require a 10′ x 10′ unit or more. Review the


[Public Storage Size Guide](https://www.publicstorage.com/size-guide) for additional options.


### **Should I Choose Drive-Up Access for Furniture Storage?**


**You should choose Drive-Up Access when you plan to move heavier furniture or make frequent trips to your unit.** Drive-Up Access brings your vehicle near select ground-level units and streamlines loading and unloading and makes frequent visit more convenient. Availability varies by location and is available at more than 2,200 of Public Storage facilities.


### **Are There Climate-Controlled Storage Units in my City Where I Can Store Furniture During Home Repairs?**


Storing furniture in a climate-controlled unit during flood damage repairs or mold remediation from water damage is useful since cities that flood often usually have high humidity. Climate-controlled storage can help keep the temperature and humidity in your unit more consistent and is useful in humid cities.


**There are climate-controlled storage units in 90% of Public Storage facilities** .
